title: Tyre and Sidon called incongruously, Ephesus congruously
source_text: CXXVIII. Deinde hoc posito dicunt Deum certos homines, exempli gratia, Tyrios & Sidonios decrevisse vocare & excitare ad conversionem, iis mediis & ea ratione, quae quidem potestatem eis revera dabant sese ad Deum convertendi si vellent, sed quae tamen certo praevidebat nullum apud ipsos effectum habitura; non vero iis mediis, quae si adhiberentur, praevidebat ipsos convertendos. Contra vero voluisse Ephesios, verbi gratia, vocare, non ea ratione quae ab ipsis respuenda esset, sed qua certo praesciebat ipsos ad fidem fore adducendos. Unde sequitur Deum decrevisse illis quidem dare gratiam, qua converti possent si vellent; at vero his gratiam qua actu converterentur.
pass_a_gloss: CXXVIII. Next, this being posited, they say that God decreed to call & rouse certain men, for example, the Tyrians & Sidonians, to conversion, by those means & in that manner, which indeed truly gave them power to convert themselves to God if they willed, but which nevertheless he foresaw for certain would have no effect with them; but not by those means, by which if they were applied, he foresaw they would be converted. But on the contrary he willed to call the Ephesians, for example, not in that manner which would be rejected by them, but in that by which he foreknew for certain they would be brought to faith. Whence it follows that God decreed to give to the former indeed grace, by which they could be converted if they willed; but to the latter grace by which they would actually be converted.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXXVIII. On that basis they say that God decreed to call and stir certain people to conversion, the Tyrians and Sidonians for example, by means and in a manner that did truly give them power to turn to God if they wished, but that he foresaw with certainty would have no effect on them. He did not call them by the means he foresaw would convert them if used.

The Ephesians, by contrast, he willed to call not in a manner they would reject, but in the one by which he foreknew for certain they would be led to faith. It follows that God decreed to give the first a grace by which they could be converted if they wished, and the second a grace by which they would in fact be converted.
